safetyCars.source: https://www.motorsportmagazine.com/archive/article/may-1993/10/cardinal-senna ('The pace car had come out on lap 30' ... 'It was lap 37 before the racing resumed')
safetyCars.note: Wikipedia has the Suzuki/Katayama crashes that caused it on lap 27; Motor Sport puts Suzuki's crash on his 28th lap and the car out on lap 30. A fan wiki table (f1.fandom) says laps 29-38. Motor Sport chosen (contemporary, gives both ends).

startTyre.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993_Brazilian_Grand_Prix ('many drivers pitted for wet tyres', Prost 'stayed out on slick tyres'); https://www.motorsportmagazine.com/archive/article/may-1993/10/cardinal-senna (the wet-tyre stops on laps 27-30 after a dry start)

slickChange.source: https://www.grandprix.com/gpe/rr534.html ('The track was drying and with the cars on wet tires it was time to pit and switch to dry ones. The man to stop first was Johnny Herbert (Lotus) and he gained a lot of places as a result. When everyone else had stopped Herbert was third behind Senna and Hill'); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993_Brazilian_Grand_Prix ('The sun then came out, it began to dry rapidly and everyone stopped for dry tyres'); https://www.motorsportmagazine.com/archive/article/may-1993/10/cardinal-senna (Herbert's stop as the safety car came in, lap 37; 'Senna made his at the end of lap 40 and Hill at the end of 41'; by lap 43 Herbert third 'as his rivals made their slick stops')
slickChange.note: Every car on wets changed back to slicks between Herbert's stop (lap 37, the first) and lap 43 (Herbert third once the others had stopped). Only Herbert's, Senna's and Hill's laps are sourced; no source read (GPE, Wikipedia, Motor Sport, formulaonehistory, flyinglap) gives any other car's lap, so the others' slick stops are estimated (reconstruct.apply_slick_change: the median sourced in-lap, 40).

runningOrder.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993_Brazilian_Grand_Prix: 'While Prost built up a substantial lead, Senna was under pressure from Hill who took second on lap 11'
https://www.motorsportmagazine.com/archive/article/may-1993/10/cardinal-senna (at the restart Hill 'leaped ahead of Senna and stretched his lead again'; 'The gap was 2.9s by lap 39')
runningOrder.note: 'by lap 39' read as the end of lap 39 (Senna's in-lap is 40)

runningOrder.source: https://www.grandprix.com/gpe/rr534.html ('When everyone else had stopped Herbert was third behind Senna and Hill, the Brazilian having taken the lead after the stop'); https://www.motorsportmagazine.com/archive/article/may-1993/10/cardinal-senna ('By lap 43, nevertheless, he had climbed to an excellent and genuine third as his rivals made their slick stops')
runningOrder.note: GPE gives the order once the slick stops were done, Motor Sport the lap Herbert was third

runningOrder.source: https://www.motorsportmagazine.com/archive/article/may-1993/10/cardinal-senna ('Hill began a counter attack that took him to a tantalising 0.199s on lap 47')
runningOrder.note: read as the end of lap 47

notes: Senna also served a 10 s stop-and-go before the rain (penalty issued on lap 25 per Wikipedia; lap served not given). Schumacher's slick stop, Alesi's two stop-and-gos (20 s and 10 s), Katayama's and Suzuki's early stops, and most slick stops: no laps. Prost (#2) stayed out and crashed on lap 29. Weather: Schumacher's lap-41 stop is a stop-and-go (no tyre change) and his slick stop has no lap, so his stint from lap 42 is estimated (slicks). Cars with no sourced wet stop run their start slicks through the rain: the snapshot invents no stops.
